transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-18    Start: 15:00 UTC    Duration: ~52m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (CTO, Hawthorn), Marcus Holt (Network), Leah Kim (Security)
---
Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
Hawthorn is evaluating Redwood private deployment options. Primary concerns: EU data residency, cross-account VPC peering vs PrivateLink, transit gateway cost, on-prem connectivity (Direct Connect/ExpressRoute), and IP/CIDR overlap. They want clear runbook and a short pilot in two regions.
---
00:00:03 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Maya from Redwood, and I have Diego, our systems engineer, with me. How's everyone doing?
00:00:09 Priya Nair: Good, thanks. Busy week but needed this one.
00:00:12 Diego Alvarez: Hi all. We'll try to keep it tight, go over the network constraints and where you want the private onramp.
00:00:20 Marcus Holt: Cool, Marcus here—I'll be hands-on for the net side. Quick note: we already have transit gateways between our prod VPCs in us-east-1 and eu-west-1, and we use a mix of Direct Connect and some VPNs for on-prem.
00:00:34 Leah Kim: Leah, security. SOC2 in process, need KMS integration for keys, and some regions we can't cross for PII.
00:00:42 Maya Chen: Great, that's helpful. High level, do you see this as a Hosted-to-Private migration or straight Private deployment behind your VPCs?
00:00:50 Priya Nair: We're leaning Private. We want integrated VPC endpoints and no internet egress for requests. But we also need the option for Redwood-hosted fallback if capacity spikes.
00:01:04 Diego Alvarez: Okay. Two paths — we can do VPC peering with our private endpoints, or PrivateLink / AWS PrivateLink style endpoints. Peering is simple but scales poorly if you have many accounts; PrivateLink gives you service endpoints in the customer's account and avoids some CIDR overlap issues.
00:01:23 Marcus Holt: CIDR overlap is the main blocker for us — several legacy accounts use overlapping 10.0/8 ranges. We also have strict /24 allocation policies in EU prod.
00:01:35 Maya Chen: Right. If you have overlapping ranges, peering is messy. Diego, can you sketch the Transit/PrivateLink tradeoff?
00:01:41 Diego Alvarez: Sure. Transit Gateway: you attach multiple VPCs and it handles routing centrally. It's great for many VPCs but adds egress hops and cost; you still need Private endpoints inside the attached VPCs if you want private service access. PrivateLink: you publish a NLB service in our managed account and you create Interface Endpoints in your account. That avoids exposing route tables between accounts but requires per-AZ ENIs and has per-GB charges. Also, latency differences are small but vary with AZ/region placement.
00:02:13 Marcus Holt: So for us, because of the overlap, PrivateLink looks better. But what about region gating? We need EU region only for some workloads. Can we force traffic to eu-west-1 endpoints?
00:02:25 Diego Alvarez: Yes. In the Redwood private control plane you can pin model variants and route by region. From the network side we expose service endpoints in each region you request. You'd create Interface Endpoints in eu-west-1 only; then traffic stays within EU.
00:02:39 Leah Kim: That sounds promising. What about key management: do we manage keys or integrate with our KMS/HSM?
00:02:46 Maya Chen: We support customer-managed keys. For Private deployments we can integrate with your KMS via IAM roles and our private control plane will use the envelope keys you register. Diego, add note on HSM?
00:02:55 Diego Alvarez: We support KMS and bring-your-own HSM for higher compliance tiers, but the integration requires some IAM permissions and the HSM must be available from the VPC or via a dedicated peering path. We'll capture the flow in the runbook.
00:03:07 Priya Nair: Good. Network egress — do you require NAT gateways outbound? Hawthorn has strict firewall egress rules and web-proxies.
00:03:15 Diego Alvarez: For interface endpoints, traffic to Redwood service flows over ENIs and doesn't need internet NAT. However, any callbacks to external systems (like telemetry) can be configured to use your egress. We can also support outbound egress through our managed nat if needed, but that exposes more surface.
00:03:30 Marcus Holt: What about IP exhaustion with ENIs? In us-east we have tight /20s per environment. If PrivateLink requires one ENI per AZ per endpoint, that adds up.
:00:03:40 Maya Chen: Yep, that's a common constraint. One mitigation is to consolidate endpoints by environment or use a single cross-account endpoint that multiple subnets route through, or use Private Service Connect on GCP if you're multi-cloud. We'll include an IP planning template.
00:03:58 Priya Nair: Multi-cloud: we have primary in AWS but GCP for analytics. Any limitations serving models from different clouds?
00:04:06 Diego Alvarez: Redwood can deploy model endpoints in both clouds. The main consideration is data residency and latency. If you pin to eu-west-1 in AWS, you need a separate deployment in europe-west1 on GCP if you want GCP-local traffic; otherwise you'd route cross-cloud and pay egress. We can discuss a hybrid topology for analytics-compute separation.
00:04:25 Leah Kim: Audit logs — do you provide audit logs for token-level request tracing? We need them for SOC2 and internal investigations.
00:04:31 Maya Chen: Yes, our Private control plane emits audit logs and per-request metadata. Logs can be exported to your SIEM via S3 or streaming (Kinesis/Streaming) depending on provider. We can also integrate with your log retention policies.
00:04:43 Marcus Holt: On the topic of performance: if we do PrivateLink in eu-west-1, can we expect comparable latencies to Hosted? We're concerned about  p99 token latency.
00:04:52 Diego Alvarez: P99 depends on a few things: model size, batch configuration, and local hardware. In most cases, local Private endpoints in the same AZ deliver p95/p99 similar to Hosted, but you'll need dedicated capacity for the tightest SLOs. For initial pilots we recommend dedicated instance pool in the region with autoscale thresholds.
00:05:12 Priya Nair: Dedicated pool sounds expensive. Can we start with hosted fallback and then move to dedicated if latency is poor?
00:05:18 Maya Chen: Absolutely. We can set routing policies: primary private endpoints, fallback to Redwood Hosted with explicit routing rules. That gives you continuity while you validate.
00:05:29 Marcus Holt: Encryption in transit — are the interface endpoints encrypted end-to-end, or does traffic terminate in your managed account?
00:05:35 Diego Alvarez: With PrivateLink the tls connection terminates at the service NLB in our managed account; from there it's routed to the serving nodes. For additional assurance we support mutual TLS between the NLB and downstream and can also do IPsec for the peering leg on request.
00:05:50 Leah Kim: Mutual TLS and KMS integration would likely satisfy this round of audits. We need to review the exact key rotation cadence.
00:05:58 Maya Chen: We'll include KMS rotation details and mTLS cert rotation schedules in the runbook.
00:06:05 Priya Nair: On compliance, we have data that can't leave EU. Do you maintain separate model shards or is the model a single global service?
00:06:13 Diego Alvarez: You can pin model variants per region — models can be hosted independently in each region so inference never leaves EU. It's part of our deployment abstraction. We'll capture the model pinning options.
00:06:24 Marcus Holt: Routing question: if we attach through our Transit Gateway, does traffic still traverse your managed account? I'm trying to avoid cross-account route table exposure.
00:06:33 Diego Alvarez: With Transit Gateway you can centralize attachments; you'd still need a mechanism to access Redwood service. We usually recommend using PrivateLink fronted by the transit for cleaner access or use VPC peering if you prefer direct VPC-VPC. But again peering exposes route tables and can complicate security groups.
00:06:52 Priya Nair: Any known gotchas for ExpressRoute/Direct Connect? We use both.
00:06:57 Diego Alvarez: BGP ASN policies and MTU differences are common gotchas. Also ensure your DC routers allow the additional prefixes (we'll provide the prefix list). For throughput tests, we can coordinate a short TCP/HTTP benchmark over your DX to measure p95/p99.
00:07:12 Marcus Holt: Good. Can you also list the firewall ports required? We have a strict allowlist model.
00:07:18 Maya Chen: Yes—will include a minimal ports list (HTTPS 443 for API, plus optional ports for control-plane agents) and the IP ranges per region.
00:07:26 Priya Nair: Timeline — we're targeting a pilot in four weeks, then a limited production roll in Q4. Is that reasonable?
00:07:33 Maya Chen: Yes, that's doable. Pilot scope: single model, eu-west-1 private endpoints, integration with customer KMS, and benchmark tests.
00:07:41 Diego Alvarez: We'll do an initial network runbook, then a handoff call with your neteng to set up interface endpoints and test.
00:07:48 Leah Kim: For the pilot, we'll need an auditors contact to review encryption details — can you share the SOC2/ISO docs?
00:07:54 Maya Chen: We'll share our security pack and redacted SOC2, and we'll open a security RACI for your auditor.
00:08:00 Marcus Holt: One more: what about IPv6 support? We're starting to require IPv6 inside eu-west.
00:08:06 Diego Alvarez: Interface Endpoints and PrivateLink support IPv6 in some cases; depends on provider. We'll confirm exact IPv6 behavior for the regions you care about and add to the runbook.
00:08:15 Priya Nair: Great. I think that's the bulk. Any blockers?
00:08:20 Maya Chen: Not from our side. We'll push the guide and set up the handoff.
00:08:25 (brief cross-talk)
00:08:28 Maya Chen: Quick recap before we close — Maya: we'll send the deployment guide, IP planning template, and security pack by tomorrow. Diego: will prepare the benchmark test plan and prefix list. Marcus: will send CIDR inventory. Priya: confirm compliance jurisdictions. Leah: will prepare a short list of audit questions for SOC2.
00:08:49 Priya Nair: Sounds good. Thanks, everyone.
00:08:51 Maya Chen: Thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the Aug 25 handoff.
00:08:55 Diego Alvarez: Bye all.
